tagline: Up Lookout Mountain to Buffalo Bill, and the long way home.
intro: Out of Golden the Lariat Trail climbs the steep east side of Lookout Mountain, five miles of road built in 1913, to the summit. From there the loop runs by Genesee to Evergreen, down Bear Creek Canyon on Highway 74 to Morrison, past Red Rocks and Dinosaur Ridge, and north on Highway 93 back to Golden.

It takes in part of the old circle drives of the Denver Mountain Parks, laid out by Frederick Law Olmsted Jr., and it has been promoted to tourists since 1914. It is still a half-day's drive from Denver.

moments.title: Lookout Mountain
moments.text: From the 7,377-foot summit downtown Denver shows plainly twelve miles east. The Utes used it as a lookout. William F. Cody is buried on top.

moments.title: Red Rocks Amphitheatre
moments.text: Ship Rock and Creation Rock make the walls of a 9,525-seat theater. Pollstar named it best small outdoor venue eleven times, then named the award after it and took it out of the running.

moments.title: Dinosaur Ridge
moments.text: In 1877 Arthur Lakes, a clergyman and teacher from Golden, found dinosaur bones in this hogback. The first Stegosaurus fossils ever identified came out of it.

practical: Part of Lookout Mountain Road closes at night.
